newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.09 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.09 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.09 percent to close at 1.0425 per dollar in the commercial forex market after the Central Bank fixed a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0425 to 1.0475, dealers said.
The previous mini-band was set Friday between 1.0415 and 1.0465 reais.
Although just a few players anticipated today's 0.1 percent lowering of the mini-band, the market reacted calmly to the change. Most players expected a Central Bank move on Thursday or Friday.

Dealers said it is still early to say whether the Central Bank is speeding up the mini-band devaluation or just concentrating reductions at the beginning of the month to improve exports, which the bank did in November and December.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.34 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.50 percent and 0.65 percent.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.1 percent to end at 1.0482. In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 0.46 percent to close at 1.100 per dollar.
